title: Backend hygiene sweep
summary: Closes five small tracked tech-debt items in one pass: a migration that backfills the auth-credentials database check onto existing databases, a shared fixture that keeps frontend and backend markdown title handling in step, removal of two make targets that can never pass, a guard test that blocks import-time database sessions, and a sharper static check for a retired dependency.
motivation: The tech-debt tracker lists five backend hygiene gaps that are cheap to close now and only get costlier as they drift.

included: backend Alembic migration chain and its integration test suite (backend/migrations, backend/tests/integration/migrations)
backend and frontend markdown title helper test suites plus one shared fixture file
backend static-enforcement tests (import-time session guard, retired-dependency grep)
the fresh-vs-brownfield divergence notes in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
excluded: behavior changes to the markdown title helpers themselves — the known divergences (frontend default title 'Untitled' vs backend 'Untitled Note', backend trimming trailing whitespace after stripping, headings not at the document start) stay as they are
repairing brownfield rows that violate the auth-credentials check — the migration fails loudly on bad data and a human decides
ticking tracker checkboxes for the other four entries — done in one follow-up commit after the binder merges, to avoid five work items colliding on one file
any UI feature or design surface

design_facts.stack: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2.0 async + PostgreSQL backend (Python 3.14 via uv); Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript frontend (Node 24 via nvm); make-driven test pipeline mirrored in Forgejo CI

isolation_params: Backend pytest is self-contained via testcontainers (per-worker PostgreSQL) but requires Docker; on this host Docker is reachable only through the Incus instance vader-incus-docker-host — stage the repo into /tmp inside it and run pytest from the ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm image with --network host, per the 'Docker-backed tests from worktrees' section of ~/AGENTS.md. CI has Docker natively.

work_items.title: Backfill the auth-credentials database check onto existing databases
work_items.summary: Add an Alembic migration so brownfield databases gain the same auth-credentials check constraint that freshly created databases already get from the model, with tests proving both the fresh and brownfield paths.

contract.migration: New revision with down_revision '1b2c3d4e5f6a' (current head). Upgrade adds a named CHECK constraint 'valid_auth_credentials' on the users table with exactly the model's predicate from backend/app/models/models.py: (auth_provider = 'local' AND password_hash IS NOT NULL) OR (auth_provider = 'oidc' AND oidc_sub IS NOT NULL). Revision id, filename, and direction are immutable once landed, per the project's migration history conventions.
contract.guards: Upgrade inspects existing check constraints on users (sa.inspect(conn).get_check_constraints) and returns early when 'valid_auth_credentials' is already present — that is the fresh-DB case where create_all built the schema first. Downgrade drops the constraint only when present and no-ops otherwise.
contract.failure_mode: If brownfield rows violate the predicate, ADD CONSTRAINT fails loudly and the migration aborts. No silent data mutation, no constraint added NOT VALID. That failure is accepted, documented behavior — a human repairs the data.
contract.tests: New integration test module follows the stamp-at-parent pattern of backend/tests/integration/migrations/test_note_tags_migration.py: (a) brownfield — stamp '1b2c3d4e5f6a', upgrade head, assert the constraint exists and an insert with auth_provider='local' and NULL password_hash is rejected; (b) fresh — create_all first, then upgrade head no-ops without error and leaves exactly one constraint; (c) downgrade drops it.
contract.docs: Update the divergence bullet in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ('Known Fresh-vs-Brownfield Divergences', currently line 168) — the check constraint is no longer fresh-only once this migration lands.

assertions: On a database stamped at revision 1b2c3d4e5f6a, alembic upgrade head adds a CHECK constraint named valid_auth_credentials on users with the model's exact predicate
On a fresh database where create_all already produced the schema, the upgrade body detects the existing constraint via the inspector and returns early without error
After upgrade, inserting a users row with auth_provider='local' and a NULL password_hash fails with an integrity error
Downgrade drops the constraint when present and no-ops when absent
The stale 'no migration creates it' claim about this constraint is gone from docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

signals: contract-mutation:db-schema — tightens the users table on brownfield databases (additive constraint, but rejects future writes that previously succeeded)
destructive-op:migration — schema migration with a downgrade that drops the constraint
sensitive-zone:migrations — backend/migrations is governed by the repo's migration history conventions (immutable ids, mandatory brownfield guards, fresh+brownfield test evidence)

work_items.title: Shared fixture keeps frontend and backend markdown titles in step
work_items.summary: One JSON file of markdown cases, imported by both test suites, so any drift between the two title helpers fails a test instead of relying on convention.

contract.fixture: New repo-root testdata/markdown-parity.json: an array of cases { name, markdown, title, stripped }. The backend test asserts extract_title(markdown) == title and remove_h1(markdown) == stripped (module functions in backend/app/utils/markdown.py) for every case; the frontend test asserts extractTitle(markdown) == title and stripTitle(markdown) == stripped (from ui/src/features/notes/noteMockHelpers.ts) for the same cases. Identical expected values on both sides — no per-side expectations.
contract.case_categories: Derived from the two implementations' actual regexes, restricted to the surface where they agree today: (1) plain first-line ATX H1 plus body; (2) H1 line with extra whitespace after the hash and trailing spaces; (3) blank lines before the H1; (4) H1-only document (stripped result is empty); (5) multiple H1s — only the first becomes the title and only the first is stripped; (6) sub-headings (##, ###) after the H1 preserved and never treated as the title; (7) hash lines inside code fences after the H1 left intact. Every case's markdown ends without trailing whitespace, because the backend trims the stripped result and the frontend does not.
contract.deliberate_exclusions: No-H1 inputs (frontend defaults to 'Untitled', backend to 'Untitled Note'), leading spaces before the hash, and H1s preceded by non-blank content are known divergences and stay out of the fixture; changing helper behavior is out of scope for this item.
contract.wiring: Backend test resolves the fixture via pathlib relative to the test file. Frontend test imports the JSON by relative path — Vitest runs in Node, so importing JSON from outside ui/ works; touch ui/tsconfig.json only if the type-checker needs resolveJsonModule enabled. Ticks the markdown-parity checkbox in docs/exec-plans/tech-debt-tracker.md (this binder's only tracker edit).

assertions: Backend pytest loads testdata/markdown-parity.json and, for every case, extract_title and remove_h1 return exactly the case's title and stripped values
Frontend Vitest imports the same JSON file and extractTitle and stripTitle return exactly the same expected values
The fixture contains at least one case in each of the seven agreed categories
Both suites read one shared file — no copied case data on either side

signals: novelty:cross-suite-fixture — first repo-root testdata/ directory and first fixture shared across the Python and TypeScript test suites; a new pattern entering the codebase, not a reuse of an existing one

work_items.title: Remove the two broken frontend auth test targets
work_items.summary: Delete the two make targets that point at React-era test files deleted in the Vue rewrite, so neither can masquerade as a runnable check.

contract.change: Remove the test-ui-oidc target (makefiles/ui.mk lines 31-35) and the test-ui-auth target (lines 37-41), each with its .PHONY declaration. Both invoke paths under ui/__tests__/features/auth/ that no longer exist and cannot return — current auth tests are colocated under ui/src/features/auth/ and OIDC validation is a backend concern. Nothing meaningful to repoint to, so removal, not repointing.
contract.unchanged: All other targets in makefiles/ui.mk stay byte-identical.

assertions: make -n test-ui-oidc exits non-zero with 'No rule to make target'
make -n test-ui-auth exits non-zero with 'No rule to make target'
make help still lists targets without error
oracle.command: ! make -n test-ui-oidc 2>/dev/null && ! make -n test-ui-auth 2>/dev/null && make help >/dev/null && make test-ui-all

work_items.title: Guard against import-time database sessions
work_items.summary: Add a test that fails whenever any backend application module constructs a database session at import time, so sessions stay request-scoped through dependency injection.

contract.rule: Every session must be request-scoped via Depends(get_async_db). The only allowed definition site for the session factory is backend/app/database/database.py (AsyncSessionLocal = async_sessionmaker(...)).
contract.test: New AST-based unit test: parse every backend/app/**/*.py with the standard-library ast module and fail if any Call whose callee name (Name or trailing Attribute) is 'AsyncSession' or 'AsyncSessionLocal' executes at import time — i.e. sits in the module or class body, outside any function or async function body — in a file other than app/database/database.py. Calls inside function bodies are allowed (seed.py constructs sessions inside functions and must keep passing). Failure message names the offending file and line. Standard library only — no new dependency.
contract.current_state: The tree already honors the rule, so the test passes as written and exists purely to stop regressions.

assertions: The new test parses every Python file under backend/app and passes on the current tree
Injecting a module-scope AsyncSessionLocal() or AsyncSession() call into any app module other than database.py makes the test fail and name the file and line
Function-scoped construction (as in seed.py) does not trip the rule

work_items.title: Sharpen the retired-dependency static check
work_items.summary: Tighten the grep that polices migration files for the retired vector-search dependency so prose mentions of its name in docstrings no longer count as violations.

contract.change: In backend/tests/integration/migrations/test_f20_static_checks.py (currently line 183), change the compiled pattern from r"from pgvector|Vector\(" to exactly r"from pgvector\.|Vector\(", and update the test's docstring so the documented rg equivalent matches the new pattern.
contract.behavior: A docstring or comment line that merely says 'pgvector' in prose no longer matches; the module-qualified import form used historically (from pgvector.sqlalchemy import Vector) and any Vector( call site still match. The scan scope (every *.py under backend/migrations/versions) and the failure message are unchanged. No migration bodies are edited.

assertions: The compiled pattern in the static-check test is exactly r"from pgvector\.|Vector\("
A line containing only the prose word pgvector does not match the new pattern; 'from pgvector.sqlalchemy import Vector' and 'Vector(' both still match
The static-check test still passes against the current migration files
